root_idea.summary: An orientation toward length, elevation, abundance, and extension of reach.
root_idea.development: The root develops from meanings of being long, full-grown, numerous, or elevated toward encompassing or applying generally; related figurative branches include covering, crowning, and extending benefit or effect broadly.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized singular kinship noun عَمّ.
The Quranic plural is normalized to the singular dictionary citation form عَمَّةٌ.

senses.definition: A paternal uncle; one's father's brother.
senses.usage_conditions: Also used in kinship expressions referring to paternal-side relatives.

senses.definition: A paternal aunt; one's father's sister.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrences are the feminine kinship counterpart of عَمّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become common, general, or universal; to include or affect people or things collectively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Can be intransitive, describing something becoming widespread, or transitive, describing its encompassing persons, things, land, or an effect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make long or tall; to become long or tall.
To become a paternal uncle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical use distinct from the kinship noun عَمّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Generalization; making something common, general, or universal, as opposed to specification.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun denoting the act or result of generalizing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a turban on someone; to wind a turban around the head.
To make someone a chief or lord, entrusting him with authority over others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from investing someone with a turban as a mark of leadership.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To equip or cover someone with a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction recorded by analogy with clothing or covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or wound someone at the head, especially at the place of the turban.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative sword construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For milk to froth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use likening the foam to a turban.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have many paternal uncles, or paternal uncles known for generosity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive and active forms are both reported for this meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To call someone a paternal uncle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or relational use in which a person is treated or addressed as an uncle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a turban, helmet, or war headgear on oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may take the turban or related headgear as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become crowned or covered, as hills with plants or mountain tops with sunlight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of turbaning or covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For vegetation to reach full height, blossom, and become luxuriant or dense.
For a young man to become tall.
For a bovine animal to have all its teeth grown.
To take or adopt someone as a paternal uncle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is someone treated as an uncle by adoption or convention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To acquire a numerous army or military force after previously having few.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare reduplicated form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company or numerous group of men, and according to some, a group from a tribe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun for a group of people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Extended paternal-side kinship, including a paternal great-uncle and paternal-cousin relations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in expressions such as ابن عمّ, whose precise degree of paternal kinship may be close or distant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tall, full-grown, abundant vegetation, especially tall palms; also herbs collectively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use applied to vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The manner of wearing a turban; in later or colloquial use, a turban itself.
The state of being gathered together and numerous or abundant.
Largeness or bigness of build.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people and other things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Completeness, full development, or absence of deficiency; by extension, a complete or fully accomplished affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a body or shoulder, a fully developed bovine animal, or an affair described as complete and generally established.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Completeness of bodily growth, stature, wealth, or youthful vigor; maturity or full development.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often used in the construction اِسْتَوَى عَلَى عُمُمِهِ, describing attainment of completeness or maturity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Complete, full, or without deficiency; also collected and abundant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective may describe a thing or a plentiful collection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Reaching or extending to everything; pervasive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded especially of perfume.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tall or complete in stature and build.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man, plant, palm tree, girl, or young woman where the source explicitly records those uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The purest, choicest, or main stock of a group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression مِنْ عَمِيمِهِمْ, synonymous with being of their main stock or finest part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dry barleygrass of the species called بُهْمَى.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical botanical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A turban, the cloth wound around the head; by extension, a helmet or similar headgear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The helmet sense is recorded as a figurative extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A raft made of pieces of wood bound together for travel on the sea or across a river.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is reported under this entry, but the source also states that the corrected form may be عَامَةٌ rather than the geminated spelling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relating to a paternal uncle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective derived from عَمّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the common sort; ordinary or vulgar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The spelling and analysis of this rare form are reported with uncertainty in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pride, haughtiness, or arrogance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Variant vocalizations are recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Companies of people in a scattered or dispersed state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural form for which no singular is supplied in the entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Common, general, universal, or comprehensive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial adjective of عَمَّ, often contrasted with خَاصّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A general term whose single application covers all items to which it applies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A grammatical or logical technical usage, distinguished from a homonym, a restricted numeral, or an indeterminate plural.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The common people, commonalty, or generality of people, as opposed to the distinguished or particular group.
Generally, collectively, or universally; sometimes the greater part or the whole of a specified period.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Examples include the greater part of a month and the whole of a day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A general or universal drought.
The resurrection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized designation based on its association with universal death before the resurrection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of or relating to the common people; common or vulgar, especially of a word or expression.
More or most general or comprehensive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used comparatively of a word or expression in respect of breadth of signification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick, full-sized, or complete in build.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded of the middle of a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having many or generous paternal uncles; in the fuller expression, having generous paternal and maternal uncles.
Good or very good in a way that extends goodness and abundant bounty to people generally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet emphasizing inclusive generosity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Turbaned or wearing a turban.
A chief or lord invested with authority over a people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from being turbaned as a mark of leadership.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having white markings on the head, forelock, or ears while the neck remains unmarked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to horses and other animals, including a sheep or goat with a white head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having abundant and tall vegetation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a meadow or similar tract of land.

cautions: The Lane discussion of عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ identifies a grammatical contraction of عَنْ مَا, not a lexical Quranic occurrence of this root.
The raft meaning reported around عِمَامَةٌ is retained with the source's explicit uncertainty over whether the form is عَمَّةٌ or the corrected عَامَةٌ.
The rare form عُمِّيّ is included, but its spelling and lexical analysis are reported as uncertain in the supplied evidence.
